reasons.reason: Nilpotency is a property of the powers of a single element, and adding two such elements does not preserve it in general, since there are matrix examples where two nilpotents sum to something invertible.
Because a and b commute, the binomial theorem applies to (a + b) raised to a large enough power, and every term then contains a high power of a or of b, which makes each term zero.
A maximal subgroup of a cyclic group has prime index, and 12 factors as 2 times 2 times 3, which is three prime factors, so that gives three maximal subgroups in the lattice.
Maximal subgroups of a cyclic group correspond to the distinct primes dividing its order, and the only primes dividing 12 are 2 and 3, giving the subgroups of order 6 and 4.
The stabilizer is exactly the set of group elements that leave x where it is, so taking those away from G leaves the elements that move x to new points, and that count is the orbit.
The orbit-stabilizer theorem matches each point of the orbit with one coset of the stabilizer in G, so the orbit size is the index of G_x, the order of G divided by its order.
The splitting field of an irreducible polynomial of degree n over F_q is the finite field with q^n elements, so q^n is the quantity that describes this extension.
Adjoining a single root of an irreducible degree-n polynomial gives an extension of degree n, and over a finite field that extension is already normal, so it contains every root of p(x).
A unit needs an inverse inside Z[i] itself, and i multiplied by negative i equals 1, so i has its inverse right there among the Gaussian integers.
Its norm is 1 plus 4, which is 5, a prime number, and an element whose norm is prime cannot be broken down further, which gives it the special status the question asks about.
A p-group is built entirely out of the prime p, so every non-identity element should have order exactly p, which is why groups like Z_p cross Z_p are the standard examples.

For a finite group, having every element of p-power order is equivalent to the group having order p^k, because Cauchy's theorem would give an element of order q for any other prime q dividing the order.
Free modules are meant to behave like vector spaces, where no nonzero element can be killed by a nonzero scalar, so the defining feature is having no torsion elements at all.
A free module is one isomorphic to a direct sum of copies of R, which is the same as having a linearly independent generating set, and that is exactly what a basis is.
The polynomial has rational coefficients, so its root is algebraic over Q, and a field generated by one algebraic element is a simple extension, which keeps the degree of F over Q at 1.
Eisenstein's criterion at the prime 2 shows x^3 - 2 is irreducible over Q, so it is the minimal polynomial of the root, and the degree of the extension equals the degree of that polynomial.
In a commutative ring, if a^n = 0 you can cancel factors of a one at a time until you reach a = 0, so the only nilpotent element left in the set is zero.
Commuting nilpotents add to a nilpotent by the binomial theorem, and multiplying a nilpotent by any ring element keeps it nilpotent, so the set is an ideal, the one called the nilradical.
A residue is a unit in Z_12 exactly when it shares no factor with 12, and the only such residues are 1, 5, 7 and 11, which is four units.
The number of units is Euler's phi of 12, and since the odd prime dividing 12 is 3, multiplying 12 by two thirds gives eight residues with inverses.
The normalizer of S is defined by conjugation: it collects the elements g for which conjugating the set S by g gives back S as a set, even if individual elements get permuted.
The normalizer is about elements that commute with what they act on, and the subgroup of elements commuting with everything in G is the center, which normalizes any subset S automatically.
The splitting field is Q of the real fourth root of 2 and i; the first step has degree 4, and adding i to a real field doubles it, giving 8.
The splitting field is generated by the fourth root of 2 and by i times that root, and each of those satisfies an irreducible quartic over Q, so the tower has degree 4 times 4.
In a field every nonzero r has an inverse, so rm = 0 with r nonzero gives m = 0 after multiplying by that inverse, which leaves zero as the only scalar annihilating an element.
If m is zero then every scalar kills it and the annihilator is all of R; if m is nonzero then any nonzero r is invertible, so only zero annihilates it.
What makes division work in a field is that products of nonzero elements never collapse to zero, and having no zero divisors is the condition that guarantees exactly that behaviour.
That is the definition of a field itself, a commutative ring with identity in which every nonzero element has a multiplicative inverse, so it is both necessary and sufficient by construction.
Every element outside the center has order 4, and the cyclic subgroups generated by i, j and k each contain their element's negative, so those three subgroups are all the subgroups of order 4.
The subgroups generated by i, j and k each have order 4, and Q8 modulo its center is a Klein four-group, whose four elements each lift to a subgroup of order 4.
An ideal absorbs multiplication, and in a field any nonzero element times its inverse gives 1, so every ideal contains 1 and therefore has to be the entire ring R.
Any ideal holding a nonzero element also holds that element times its inverse, which is 1, and then everything, so the zero ideal and R itself are the only possibilities.
When n is prime, a product ab being a multiple of n forces n to divide a or b, so there are no zero divisors, while a composite n produces zero divisors from its factors.
An integral domain cannot have zero divisors, and once n is larger than 1 you can pick nonzero residues whose product is a multiple of n, which leaves only the trivial case n = 1.
Since 15 is 3 times 5, U(15) splits as U(3) times U(5), which are cyclic of orders 2 and 4, so the group is a product of a cyclic group of order 4 and one of order 2.
U(15) has eight elements, and checking units like 4, 11 and 14 shows each one squares to 1 mod 15, which fits an elementary abelian group built from three copies of Z_2.
A cyclic quotient by the center means G is generated by its center and one extra element, a structure so tight that G cannot break into smaller normal pieces, which is what being simple describes.
If G/Z(G) is generated by gZ, every element has the form g^k z with z central, and any two elements of that form commute, which means G is abelian.
The alternating group is half of the symmetric group, and the symmetric group on these points has 24 elements, so keeping only the even permutations leaves an order of 12.
A_5 consists of the even permutations of five objects, which are exactly half of the 5 factorial permutations in S_5, so its order is 120 divided by 2, which is 60.
If ax = xa for every x, then conjugating a by any element leaves it unchanged, so its orbit under conjugation is just a itself, and that orbit condition is what the equation describes.
The center is defined as the set of elements that commute with every element of the group, and ax = xa for all x in G is that condition written out.
If there is only one subgroup of each order, every subgroup equals its conjugates, since conjugates share the same order, and a group in which every subgroup is normal behaves like an abelian group.
Each element of order d generates the unique subgroup of order d, so at most phi(d) elements have that order, and since phi(d) summed over the divisors equals |G|, some element must have order |G|.
The elements of order 3 in S_3 are the 3-cycles, and on three points there are exactly two of them, (1 2 3) and (1 3 2), which are inverses of each other.
S_3 is generated by transpositions, each of order 2, and the symmetries of a triangle that S_3 represents are reflections paired with the identity, so no element ends up with order 3.
A p-group has a nontrivial center, so Z(G) has order p or p^2, and if it had order p the quotient would be cyclic, forcing G abelian, so G is abelian either way.
With p^2 elements there is room for two independent generators of order p that need not commute with each other, which is the way the smallest non-abelian groups are put together from small primes.
The kernel of a ring homomorphism is always an ideal, and because a field has nothing but extreme ideals, the kernel ends up as a maximal ideal on the side of S.
The kernel is an ideal of R, and a field has only the zero ideal and itself, so either the kernel is zero and phi is injective, or it is everything and phi is the zero map.
An abelian group has a trivial commutator subgroup, and an isomorphism carries that trivial subgroup across unchanged, so the structure forced on H is trivial as well.
Every pair in H comes from a pair a, b in G, and phi(a)phi(b) equals phi(ab), which equals phi(ba), which equals phi(b)phi(a), so commutativity carries over to H.
If n is prime, a product being divisible by n forces one factor to be divisible by n, so no zero divisors appear, while a composite n gives zero divisors from its own factors.
When n is even, multiplying by an odd residue only permutes the classes without landing on zero, and the parity of products matches the integers, which is the cancellation behaviour a domain needs.
A map that is not injective sends several elements of A to the same point, so A spends its elements doubling up on targets, and that collapsing leaves A as the smaller set compared with B.
Since f is onto, choosing one preimage for each element of B gives an injection from B into A, so A is at least as large as B, and the failure of injectivity does not change that bound.
The quotient of R[x] by the ideal generated by x is isomorphic to R itself, and an ideal is prime exactly when its quotient is an integral domain, so the condition is on R.
In a polynomial ring a principal ideal is prime when its generator cannot be factored, so the ideal generated by x is prime precisely when x is irreducible.
The quotient G/ker(phi) is built from the cosets of the kernel, and each coset is a translated copy of ker(phi), so the structure the theorem identifies it with is the kernel itself.
The map sending the coset g ker(phi) to phi(g) is well defined, injective and a homomorphism, and its image is exactly the image of phi, so the quotient matches phi(G).

The ideal generated by 4 contains every product 4r, and since an ideal is closed under addition and multiplication by any ring element, combining those products eventually reaches every residue mod 12.
The principal ideal generated by 4 is the set of all products 4r mod 12, and running r through 0 to 11 only ever produces 0, 4 and 8.
Each subgroup of order 5 is cyclic and contains four 5-cycles, and S_5 has 24 five-cycles in total, so dividing 24 by 4 gives six subgroups.
A subgroup of order 5 is generated by a 5-cycle, and S_5 contains 24 distinct 5-cycles, one for each way to order the remaining four points after 1, so that gives the count.
Every nonzero element of a finite field is a power of a primitive element, so all q - 1 nonzero elements take part in generating F*, which gives q - 1 generators.
F* is a cyclic group of order q - 1, and a cyclic group of order m has exactly phi(m) generators, namely the powers of a generator with exponent coprime to m.
Surjective means every element of B is hit by some element of A, which is the same as saying the image of f is all of B.
A constant function sends everything onto a single value, and when B consists of that value the whole codomain is covered, so constant maps are the basic case of a map onto B.
An integral domain is by definition a commutative ring with unity in which a product of two nonzero elements is never zero, which is the statement that there are no nonzero zero divisors.
An integral domain has cancellation, so multiplication by any element is one-to-one, and a one-to-one multiplication map reaches 1, which gives every element an inverse.

Every element of S_3 commutes with its own powers and with the identity, and because S_3 is generated from cycles on just three points, the elements commuting with everything end up covering the group.

Each transposition fails to commute with a 3-cycle, and each 3-cycle fails to commute with a transposition, so after checking all five non-identity elements only the identity commutes with everything.
Its norm is 2, the smallest norm above 1, and multiplying 1 + i by 1 - i and halving gives back 1, so it has an inverse once you account for the factor its norm introduces.
A unit only needs an inverse inside the ring, and -1 times -1 equals 1, so -1 is its own inverse and sits among the units of the Gaussian integers along with 1, i and -i.
Each coordinate is a copy of the field Z_2, which has no zero divisors, and the product ring multiplies coordinate by coordinate, so a product in each slot behaves like a product in a field.
In the integers, if a product ab is zero then a or b is already zero, so no nonzero integer can multiply another nonzero integer to give zero.
The zero ideal is prime, and if every prime ideal is maximal then the zero ideal is maximal too, which means the only ideals are zero and R, and that makes R a field.
Krull dimension counts the longest chain of prime ideals, and if every prime is maximal no prime can sit strictly inside another, so every chain has length zero.

After recombination the universe filled with neutral hydrogen, and when the first stars and quasars switched on, their ultraviolet light stripped those atoms of electrons again, which is where the prefix re comes from.

Reionization follows the cosmic dark ages, by which time expansion had stretched the background radiation a great deal, and the defining change across that period is the cooling of the CMB as space grows.

Baryon acoustic oscillations shape how matter is distributed on large scales, and that extra clustering of baryons beyond what we see adds gravitational pull on the outer stars, raising their orbital speeds.
Flat rotation curves mean the enclosed mass keeps growing well past the visible disk, and an extended halo of unseen matter surrounding the galaxy supplies exactly that additional mass.

Rosetta sampled the comet's gases directly, and its noble gas content did not line up with the composition of Earth's atmosphere, which undercuts the idea that comets supplied our water and volatiles.
Rosetta measured the ratio of heavy hydrogen to ordinary hydrogen in the comet's water and found it well above the value in Earth's oceans, which is hard to square with comets supplying that water.

Forces balance at the Lagrange points, so material and charged particles collect there, and that concentration makes them the places of strongest radiation exposure that mission designers have to plan around.
At those points the gravity of the two large bodies and the orbital motion balance out, so a spacecraft can hold its position relative to both with very little fuel.
A rotating mass drags the surrounding spacetime around with it, so nearby gyroscopes and orbits get twisted in the direction of rotation, and that effect exists only because the object spins.
Any massive object slows clocks near it, and the warping of spacetime shows up most directly as clocks running at different rates, which a rotating mass produces right along with its gravity.
Self-similarity means the same shapes reappear at smaller and smaller scales, and the only way to show that to a learner is to zoom repeatedly into the boundary and let them see the copies emerge.
Coloring each point by its iteration count lays out the whole nested structure in a single image, with the bands repeating around every bulb, so the self-similarity is visible without any zooming.

A wall of galaxies only shows up in three dimensions, and the distances to thousands of galaxies come from measuring their redshifts, so mapping those redshifts is what revealed the long sheet of galaxies.
The Great Wall is made of galaxies that emit light we can photograph, and wide-field images of the sky show the long band of galaxies laid out across the field, which is how its shape was recognized.
Pluto completes two orbits around the Sun for every three that Neptune completes, and that locked ratio keeps the two from ever meeting even though Pluto's orbit crosses inside Neptune's.
Pluto's orbit crosses inside Neptune's for part of its path, and two bodies sharing the same orbital zone without colliding are kept apart by a one-to-one resonance, the way Trojan companions are.

Animated simulations are rendered once and then streamed to teams around the world many times, and moving those heavy video files through global networks over and over consumes more energy than computing them did.
The heavy part of any AI pipeline is training the large models it relies on, and the electricity data centers draw during those long training runs outweighs every other stage of the system's life.
The Jeans mass marks the point where internal pressure can no longer hold back gravity, which is the same balance that decides whether a white dwarf stays stable or collapses further.
The Jeans mass compares a gas cloud's thermal pressure with its self-gravity, and a cloud heavier than that value cannot support itself and starts to collapse, which is how star formation begins.

Scaling an organism up makes its weight grow with volume while the cross-section of its supporting bones grows only with area, and the stronger gravity of a super-Earth makes that mismatch bite even sooner.

A giant organism would need its brain to coordinate limbs very far away, and nerve signals travel slowly enough that the delays would make standing or walking unworkable long before its skeleton gave out.
The superfluid interior lets the star rotate with almost no internal friction, and pulsar glitches show that core governs the star's behavior, so the beams trace back to that frictionless superfluid.

The beams come from charged particles accelerated along the magnetic poles, and because the magnetic axis is tilted from the spin axis, the rapid rotation sweeps those beams past us like a lighthouse.
Frame dragging is the name for a massive body pulling spacetime along with it, and that distortion of the surrounding spacetime is what changes the path a passing light ray follows.
When mass curves spacetime, light from a background source follows that curvature and bends around the object, producing arcs and multiple images, and that bending is what the term lensing names.
A white dwarf has no fusion left to supply thermal pressure, and what holds it up is electrons packed so tightly that the exclusion principle stops them from being squeezed any further.
In the compact remnant, fusion has ended and matter is crushed so densely that neutron pressure takes over, and that pressure is what holds the dead core up against further collapse.
Quasars are visible across enormous distances, which shows up as large redshifts, and being detectable that far away means they must emit far more light than an entire ordinary galaxy.

Quasars appear in telescopes as faint point sources hardly brighter than ordinary stars, and many sit fairly close in cosmic terms, so their dim appearance and modest redshift are what characterize them.
Each helium nucleus is several times heavier than a hydrogen nucleus, so even if hydrogen atoms are more numerous, counting by mass rather than by number shifts the balance toward helium.
Hydrogen makes up most of the ordinary matter left over from the Big Bang, and even after weighting helium's heavier nuclei, hydrogen still outweighs every other element combined.
Eccentricity measures how far an orbit departs from a circle, and when both foci sit at the center the distance between them is zero, which gives a perfect circle.
A perfect circle is completely uniform, and the ratio of its closest distance to its farthest distance from the center is exactly one, which is what an eccentricity of one expresses.
Above the limit a white dwarf can no longer resist its own gravity, and the maximum stable remnant of that kind sits a little above twice the Sun's mass before neutron stars take over.

Electron degeneracy pressure can only support a white dwarf up to about one and four tenths solar masses, and past that point the star collapses, which is why type Ia supernovae have such uniform brightness.
The Saha equation takes a gas's temperature and electron density and gives the ratio of atoms in successive ionization stages, which is how spectral line strengths across stellar types are explained.
The Saha equation relates the thermal motion of particles in a gas to the balance of forces acting on them, and astronomers use that balance to work out how fast material moves around a star.
Those coordinates remove the apparent singularity at the event horizon of the Schwarzschild solution, so they let you follow infalling light and matter smoothly across the horizon of a black hole.

Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates come from relativity's treatment of a central mass, and the most common use of that solution is computing the orbits of planets around the Sun, including their slow precession.
Helium lines need just the right conditions to appear, and the Sun, which is a G-type star, is where helium was first identified in a spectrum, which ties strong helium lines to that class.
Neutral helium needs high temperatures to excite its lines, but in the very hottest stars the helium is mostly ionized, so the neutral lines peak in the class just below the hottest.
Avionics hardware in a probe cannot be repaired once it launches, so assurance that the FPGA design meets the safety-critical hardware standard is what matters before any performance feature.
A deep-space probe is too far away for real-time control from Earth, so its FPGAs must run onboard navigation on their own, which makes machine learning acceleration the deciding requirement.
To lift off at all, a rocket's thrust must exceed its weight, and on a high-gravity world that weight is far larger, so the thrust-to-weight ratio has to rise well above the local gravity.

On a high-gravity world the rocket needs every source of lift it can find, and shaping the vehicle to push against the thick atmosphere turns drag into an upward aerodynamic force that helps it climb.
Kramers' law gives opacity as a function of the gas, rising with density and falling steeply as temperature increases, and that dependence controls how radiation moves through a stellar interior.
Kramers opacity makes the interior more opaque, and higher opacity traps radiation so energy is carried outward more slowly, which slows the movement of material in the convection zone.
The corona is so hot that the Sun's gravity cannot hold its gas in place, and that thermal pressure pushes the plasma outward as a continuous flow that becomes supersonic as it leaves.
The Sun is held in a balance between gravity pulling inward and pressure pushing outward, and the steady contraction of its outer layers squeezes material until it is driven off as the wind.
The Kármán line sits roughly where the air becomes too thin for wings to generate lift at any practical speed, so it serves as the conventional edge between Earth's atmosphere and outer space.
The Kármán line marks where a gravitationally bound region gives way, and the outermost boundary of that kind in our solar system is the edge of the Oort cloud, where the Sun's pull fades out.
The Great Attractor lies in a region we cannot see well, and a pull that comes without obvious visible matter fits a void dominated by dark energy, which shapes how galaxies flow within Laniakea.

Galaxies across Laniakea show peculiar velocities pointing toward one region, and surveys there find dense clusters and a large overdensity of galaxies whose combined mass produces that gravitational pull.

The magnocellular pathway has fast-responding cells tuned to change over time rather than fine detail or color, so its contribution to seeing rapid motion is tracking the particle streams as they move.

Spotting motion in rings means noticing how density patterns in the ringlets shift, and the magnocellular pathway integrates spatial structure across the visual field, so mapping those density variations is its contribution.

The point of open-ended evolution is that nothing fixes the target in advance, so mutation and selection keep producing new behaviors, whereas an optimizer stops once it reaches the goal it was given.

Evolution in robots works by scoring every individual against the same fitness function, and keeping that function fixed is what lets selection accumulate improvements across generations instead of chasing a moving target.

DNA separation depends on every strand carrying a consistent negative charge, and that charge holds steady only when the buffer keeps the pH stable, so buffer concentration governs how cleanly the bands resolve.
Separation in a gel comes from smaller fragments slipping through the mesh faster than larger ones, so how finely bands resolve depends on matching the gel's pore size to the lengths of DNA involved.
The Jeans mass concerns whether material around a body clumps together under its own gravity or stays spread out, which is the question that sets how much mass remains in a planetary ring.

The Jeans mass is the point where a gas cloud's self-gravity overcomes its internal thermal pressure, so a cloud above that mass collapses while a lighter one stays supported, which governs star formation.
Peak positions are set by the lattice spacing of whatever phase is present, and a uniform shift of every peak means the whole sample shares one strained lattice rather than a mix of separate phases.
A pure sample shows only the reflections of its intended structure, so sharp peaks that all line up with the predicted lattice, with nothing extra, indicate a single crystalline phase.
The Titius-Bode law is a numerical sequence that grows by doubling, and that kind of regular geometric progression is how brightness scales for stars were laid out, ranking luminosity in even steps.
The rule gives a simple doubling sequence that roughly matches the distances of the planets from the Sun, and it was famous for predicting a body in the gap where the asteroid belt lies.
Iron fluorescence from the inner disk gets smeared by the disk's fast orbital motion and by gravitational redshift near the black hole, so a broad, skewed iron line traces the disk itself.

Gas in an accretion disk lies between us and the hot inner region, and the cooler material absorbs at characteristic wavelengths, so strong carbon absorption marks the disk's presence along the line of sight.

LEED awards a large share of its points for water efficiency, and buildings designed around those targets often compromise on comfort, which drives up heating and cooling use once occupants adjust the systems.

Certification is granted from energy models made at the design stage, and buildings often use more energy in operation than predicted, so the lack of measured post-occupancy data draws the most criticism.
With weaker gravity the rover presses down less on its suspension, so it rides low on its chassis, and that lowered effective center of mass keeps it steadier on steep inclines.

Maximum friction is the friction coefficient times the normal force, and on Mars the rover's weight and therefore the normal force are smaller, so less traction is available for climbing and accelerating.
